title: Clever octopuses
text:
An octopus is one of the strangest animals in the sea. It has no bones at all, and its soft body is made of muscle. The only hard part is its beak, so even a big octopus can ooze through a gap not much wider than that beak. This helps it to hide in cracks between rocks.

An octopus has eight arms, and each arm is covered in round suckers. The suckers can grip, but they can also taste and feel. An octopus also has three hearts. Two of them pump blood past the gills, and the third pumps blood around the rest of the body. Its blood is blue, not red.

Octopuses are famous for changing colour. Special cells in their skin let them turn red, brown, white or speckled in less than a second. This helps them to hide from sharks and other hunters. If an enemy comes close, an octopus may squirt out a cloud of dark ink and then dart away while the hunter cannot see.

Scientists have found that octopuses are very good at solving problems. In laboratories, some have learned to unscrew the lid of a jar to reach a crab inside. Others have found their way through a maze.

Most octopuses live alone, and many kinds live for only one or two years. In my opinion, that is a pity, because they are such clever and interesting animals. Still, scientists keep studying them, and every year they discover something new.
